newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Wiener St'sche says sees record year.
newsitem.headline: Wiener St'sche says sees record year.

text.p: Austrian insurer Wiener Staedtische Allgemeine Versicherung AG said on Thursday premium income rose 14.4 percent in the first eight months of 1996 and that it was on course for a record year.
Premium income rose to 12.7 billion schillings, boosted by a 48.9 percent jump in life insurance to 4.8 billion schillings, the firm said in a statement.
"Wiener Staedtische remains firmly on its successful course," said chief executive Siegfried Sellitsch.
Wiener Staedtische reiterated that premium income for the full year should reach 17 billion schillings, up from 16.4 billion in 1995.
Profit based on OeVFA accounting standards should rise to 1.05 billion schillings from 1.02 billion in 1995, the company continued.
Damage and accident premium income rose 1.3 percent to 5.7 billion schillings in the first eight months of the year, despite price competition in the car insurance market.
But new rules for health insurance categories led to a 1.3 percent decline in health premium income to 2.2 billion schillings, Wiener Staedtische said.
Insurance payments climbed 7.7 percent to 6.9 billion schillings, while operating expenses rose 4.2 percent to 2.9 billion, the company said.
